No offset or permutation is applied and none is needed: for 30 of the 33 previously-refused verses the coordinate-aligned source row is also the single best text match among all 1,975 source rows, the runner-up scoring at or below 0.64, so there is no numbering divergence in the Yajurveda. Two defects in the shipped matcher were corrected before scoring -- see docs/reports/data-completeness/audio-yv.md, section 'Two instrument defects'. The corrected instrument was recalibrated over all 1,975 coordinate-aligned pairs (median 1.0000, p5 0.9862) against 800 deliberately mispaired ones (median 0.2514, max 0.5690), and it re-accepts every verse the shipped matcher accepted -- zero regressions.
prior_automated_checks.recension_evidence: Madhyandina specifically, on three converging structural facts plus this row's own text. (2) IGNCA's own page titled 'Yajurveda, Madhyandina Samhita, Adhyaya 01' enumerates mantras 1-31, and this corpus's adhyaya 1 holds exactly 31 mantras. (3) Per row: the text the source states this recording recites is this corpus's Madhyandina text for the same coordinate at the orthography-insensitive skeleton similarity recorded in payload.text_match_score, which is at or above 0.9777 for every accepted row. This is NOT a publisher label: the source names no recension anywhere. It is a positive identification from structure and per-mantra text, and it is the reason the 54-part / ~37 h 'Shukla Yajurveda' archive.org family was rejected rather than used.

prior_automated_checks.mapping_method: The dataset publishes no kanda.sukta.mantra key, so the key was established from the sample's own published transcript and the dataset's own ordering, and from nothing else. Four conditions had to hold together: the transcript is letter-identical to this corpus's Saunaka text for VG:AV:SAU:K20:S128:V015; the sample is filed under kanda 20, which is this mantra's kanda; its running index 40202 falls between the indices of this mantra's nearest letter-identical neighbours in the same kanda, so the dataset's own ordering agrees with the text match; and it is the only sample in that window reciting this text. The boundary is the file boundary -- one standalone WAV containing exactly this mantra -- so no timestamp is asserted. No ASR was run: the transcript is the dataset's own published metadata.
prior_automated_checks.recension_evidence: Per row: the sample's published Devanagari transcript is letter-identical to this corpus's Saunaka PRIMARY_TEXT for VG:AV:SAU:K20:S128:V015 (Roth & Whitney, Berlin 1856). At corpus level, 9,034 of the dataset's 9,997 Atharvavedic transcripts are exact letter-substrings of the Saunaka samhita text and 773 are letter-identical to a whole Saunaka mantra across all 20 kandas; a Paippalada corpus could not achieve letter-exact containment at that rate. The dataset itself states no recension, so this is the only evidence, and it is textual rather than editorial.
